fault_notes: No faults planted. The agent verifies identity, investigates the evening disconnections, acknowledges Hannah's frustration, and confirms that the connection remains working after correcting the scheduled Wi-Fi setting.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net. You're speaking with Jo in broadband support. Can I take your name and hear what's been happening?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's Hannah Davies. Our broadband keeps dropping every evening. It's fine during the day, then suddenly nothing works, usually just when we're settling down to watch something.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hi Hannah. Having it disappear when you finally get time to use it sounds really annoying. Could you give me the first line of your address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's 18 Willow Crescent. The account should be under my name. We moved here in March, if that makes any difference.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's matched, thank you. So your connection behaves normally through the day, but cuts out in the evenings across the things you're using. Have I understood?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. And honestly, I'm getting fed up. My daughter lost part of an online lesson yesterday. We're paying for something we can't rely on when we actually need it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm sorry it interrupted her lesson. I understand why you're losing patience with it. I'll work through this with you. When did you first notice the evening pattern?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Monday, I think. No, Sunday night was the first time. It's happened every night since. It goes off around eight, though I haven't timed it exactly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That regular timing is useful. When it happens, what do the router lights do, and does your Wi-Fi name disappear or stay visible without internet?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The big light stays white. There's a smaller wireless light that goes out. Our network disappears from my phone, actually. I'd assumed that just meant the broadband was gone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's a helpful distinction. It could be the wireless signal switching off while the line stays connected. Which devices are affected, and is anything connected with a cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Both phones, my daughter's laptop and the television. They're all wireless. There's an old desktop upstairs with a cable, but we hardly ever switch that on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can leave the desktop for now. What have you already tried when the wireless disappears? I'll avoid making you repeat steps that haven't helped.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've switched the router off at the wall twice. It comes back for a little bit after starting up, then disappears again. I haven't pressed the little reset button.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thanks, leave that reset button alone for now. Did anything change around Sunday, perhaps a router update, a new device, or someone adjusting settings in the app?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My partner was looking at bedtime controls for the children's tablets. He said he'd only been looking, though. We've had no new equipment, and nobody mentioned an update.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: There are separate controls for individual devices and the whole wireless network, so we'll check which is set. Are you calling on your mobile, rather than the home phone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, my mobile. I've got mobile data on as well. It's nearly eight now, so we're probably about to see it happen again while we're talking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We can use that to check the pattern directly. Please open the S-Net app on your mobile and select your home broadband account. What options appear underneath?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, it's asking for my fingerprint. Okay, I'm in. There's connection status, manage Wi-Fi, connected devices, and something about family controls underneath those.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Choose manage Wi-Fi, please, then look for a schedule or wireless timer. Don't change anything yet; I'd like to establish exactly what's currently enabled before we alter it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh. There's a schedule switched on. It says pause Wi-Fi, every day, from twenty hundred until six in the morning. That's eight, isn't it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, eight in the evening. That setting pauses the whole wireless network overnight, which fits the disappearing name and light. Is the schedule labelled all Wi-Fi or selected devices?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All Wi-Fi. Oh, there it goes now, the little light's gone out. Honestly, three evenings of this because of one switch. That's really frustrating.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can understand that, especially after the disrupted lesson and those restarts. The controls are easy to confuse. We'll remove this schedule and check everything reconnects properly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, please. I don't want the whole house cut off every night. Will switching this off erase the Wi-Fi password or anything we've already connected?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, it leaves your network name and password as they are. Turn off that schedule and press save. Let me know whether you get a confirmation or error.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Done. There's a spinning circle. Right, that's stopped, and a green message says settings saved. The schedule switch is grey now instead of purple.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good. While that reaches the router, open the Wi-Fi settings on your phone. Watch for your usual network to return; there's no need to restart anything.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The wireless light's back already. And there's our network, Davies Home. It's connected by itself, but my phone sometimes uses mobile data when the Wi-Fi isn't working.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exactly, so let's make sure we're testing the home connection. Leave Wi-Fi on, temporarily switch mobile data off, and try opening a webpage you haven't just visited.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Mobile data's off. I'll try the garden centre website, I've been meaning to check their hours. Yes, that's loaded, and another page opens when I tap it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms internet access over Wi-Fi on your phone. Could you also try playing something on the television, so we check another device rather than relying on one?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The remote's under a cushion, naturally. Here we go. I'll put the news on through the app. It's started straight away, no connection warning this time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Leave that playing while we check the saved setting once more. You can turn mobile data back on afterwards. Does the app still show the wireless schedule disabled?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's still off. I went back a screen and opened it again to make sure. The television's still playing behind me. My daughter's laptop has reconnected too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's encouraging, Hannah. We've passed the scheduled cutoff and restored the devices without a restart. Would you prefer to leave all bedtime controls off for the moment?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Definitely. We can discuss the children's tablets another time. I'd rather have a working connection tonight than start experimenting with more settings while everyone's using it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That's absolutely fine. We won't change anything else. I'm adding a note that the whole-network evening schedule was disabled and your phone, television and laptop reconnected.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks. I was worried you'd say we needed an engineer and I'd have to take time off. Is there anything here that suggests the router itself is faulty?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What we've observed points to the schedule: the wireless stopped at its set time and returned when you disabled it. We haven't seen evidence requiring a router replacement today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes sense. The television hasn't stopped once. My daughter says her lesson recording is playing as well, so she's catching up on the bit she missed.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm glad she can catch up. To confirm before we finish, is the connection issue now resolved, with your devices online and no further drops since that change?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it's fixed now. Everything's online and staying connected. We've definitely got past eight, which was when it vanished before. That's a relief, honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Great, the issue is resolved on our checks today. We've removed the daily wireless pause, kept your existing password, and confirmed working internet on several devices after the cutoff.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Lovely. And that stays off tomorrow as well, doesn't it? I don't need to come back into the app every evening and switch it off again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Correct, it stays disabled unless someone enables it again. If another drop occurs, contact us and we'll investigate using today's notes. You don't need to make any further changes tonight.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Brilliant. I'll let my partner know which setting it was, without giving him too much grief. Thanks for sticking with me and explaining what we were actually checking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You're welcome, Hannah. I hope you all get a peaceful evening with it working again. Thank you for choosing S-Net. Enjoy the rest of your evening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks, Jo. You too. I'll finally get back to my programme. Bye.
